reading.title: Maps that tell stories
reading.text: Traditional geography lessons asked students to memorise capital cities. Today, teachers use interactive graphics instead. A single map can show demographic change across a century: where young families moved, which villages emptied, how cities grew. Old photographs add a human dimension, and short biographies of local people turn data into stories. Several schools have joined a national programme that trains teachers to build these digital maps. Early results suggest that students not only remember more facts but also understand why places change.
